newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares slip but trading healthy- brokers.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares slip but trading healthy- brokers.

text.p: Egyptian share prices slipped a fraction in active trading on Tuesday but brokers wrote off the decrease as negligible and said the market was consolidating in preparation for an uptrend.
"The market is better, there's lots of demand. Prices have dropped to a very attractive level and that is tempting back many investors," said broker Sherif Cararah at EFG-Hermes.
"Today's fall is nothing. I have a very positive feeling that it will rise," he added.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index fell 0.47 points to 333.23 points -- its lowest level since mid-January. Turnover was a healthy 64.00 million pounds ($18.85 million).
"The market is currently consolidating but it will definitely go up," said Bassim Arida, an analyst at Prime Investments.
"There are some investors who are actively buying in the market but the price slippages were caused by others who got jittery and sold out towards the end," he added.
The blue-chip cement firms and banks were among the day's most active shares but the market also saw heavy trading in a mixed bag of stocks.

Mohandes Insurance was the day's busiest stock, trading more than 13.8 million pounds and brokers attributed the unusual activity to rumours that a Saudi investor was trying to buy out the firm. Shares ended 2.23 pounds higher at 47.

Monopoly brewer al-Ahram Beverages, also known as Pyramids Breweries, was active with 3.83 million pounds of turnover. "Mainly foreign investors are buying the local shares because they are cheaper than the firm's GDR," Cararah said.
Al-Ahram's global depository receipts are listed on the London stock exchange.
Real estate firms Medinet Nasr Housing and Development and Heliopolis Housing and Development were also active in what brokers said was institutional buying.
Arab Cotton Ginning continued to be active for the second day running with 4.4 million pounds worth of trade but the share shed one pound to 59.

Among the popular cements, Suez Cement drew the most interest, rising 1.5 to 63 pounds in 4.5 million pounds worth of trade. Investors were also busy with Commercial International Bank but the share closed 0.1 pound lower at 70.15.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 443.22 points from 443.02 points on Monday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms fell to 249.99 points from 250.57 points.
Of the 80 shares traded, 25 rose, 31 ended lower and 24 remained unchanged.
